## Three paths to the neighborhood

```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
flowchart LR
  A[Microdata with postal code<br>SIH, APACs, SINASC-RJ] -->|postal code → CNEFE 2022| D[IBGE neighborhood]
  B[Regional TabNets<br>Rio, RJ state, São Paulo, Fortaleza, SC] -->|neighborhood name| C[Name matching]
  F[Open data<br>Recife, Curitiba] -->|name and postal code| C
  C --> D
  D --> E[2022 Census population<br>rate per 10,000<br>coordinates and boundaries]
```

### 1. By postal code

**CNEFE 2022** is the IBGE register of every Census address, with postal code, coordinates and census tract. The package:

1. gives each address its **official neighborhood** (through the census tract). In municipalities without official neighborhoods, it uses the **locality** written in the address;
2. gives each **postal code** the neighborhood where most of its addresses are;
3. discards postal codes that do not point to a place: generic, special, or covering several neighborhoods (see [tutorial 4](04-hospitalizations-and-zip-codes.qmd)).

The coordinates of a postal code or neighborhood are the **median** of its addresses' coordinates.

### 2. Through TabNets

TabNet is the web tabulation tool used by Brazilian health departments. Some departments publish tables by neighborhood in their TabNet. The package fills in the website form as a person would, and reads the resulting table.

| Source | Coverage | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Rio de Janeiro City Health Department (SMS-Rio) | Rio de Janeiro, since 2006 | neighborhood |
| Rio de Janeiro State Health Department (SES-RJ) | all municipalities of RJ state, neighborhoods since 2011 | neighborhood |
| São Paulo City Health Department | São Paulo | district (96) |
| Santa Catarina Epidemiological Surveillance (DIVE-SC) | all municipalities of SC state | neighborhood |
| Fortaleza City Health Department | Fortaleza, since 1999 | neighborhood |

Besides TabNets, some city halls publish **open data** with the neighborhood: arboviruses and SAMU calls in Recife and medical consultations in Curitiba (see [tutorial 8](08-consultations-samu-facilities.qmd)).

This list comes from a survey of the TabNets of all 27 states and their capitals (October 2026). Most of them stop at the municipality level.

### 3. Name matching

A TabNet only gives the neighborhood **name**, written its own way ("FREGUESIA-ILHA", "Jd. América"). The package compares it with IBGE neighborhoods **within the same municipality**, in this order:

| Step (`ligacao`) | Example |
|---|---|
| `exata`: identical name, ignoring accents, abbreviations and prepositions | "Jd. América" → Jardim América |
| `sem numeração`: without the trailing number | "Santa Rosa II" → Santa Rosa |
| `parcial`: one name contains the other | "COMPLEXO DA MARE" → Maré |
| `aproximada`: the closest name (up to 15% different) | "Cavalcante" → Cavalcanti |

The `ligacao` column records which step was used. Names that don't match are marked `não encontrado` (not found), and "Ignorado"/"Em branco" (unknown/blank) are marked `ignorado`. Nothing is dropped silently. In 2023, **99.8%** of Rio de Janeiro's deaths were linked.

You can use the same matching with any list of names:

```r
ligar_bairros(c("Jd. América", "COMPLEXO DA MARE"), "330455", "RJ")
```

## Limitations

- **Only what is public:** most places do not publish data by neighborhood.
- **TabNets change:** websites go offline or change their forms. The package retries 3 times and caches what already worked.
- **2022 population:** rates use the 2022 Census population and are crude (not age-standardized).
- **Records without neighborhood:** records without a usable postal code are left out of the numerator, so the true rate may be higher.
